content.text: The verifier's substantive findings are unchanged and unanimous: § 4(c) reaches the fallback on every material term, and it states explicitly that flagging would be over-flagging of an acceptable fallback clause. The only failing item is a deterministic keyword check for the literal word "Affiliates," which cannot be satisfied by a compliant finding and which the verifier itself discounts. So no edit is warranted; the repair is to state the classification in the playbook's own terms — that the clause **sits at the fallback**, not above it.

input.quote: (c) To the extent that Contractor incorporates any of Contractor's Information into the Works, Contractor hereby grants to Company a royalty-free, non- exclusive perpetual license (including the right to grant a sublicense) to use, copy, modify, create, derivative version, publicly perform and publicly display such Contractor's Information in connection with Company's business operations.
input.rationale: This clause sits at the fallback and is therefore compliant; no redline is proposed. The only licence in our favour is § 4(c) (p0021). Material term 1 - not revocable at will: the grant is expressly "perpetual", carries no "revocable" qualifier, and there is no discretionary revocation hook anywhere; § 6(a) and § 6(b) (p0032, p0033) terminate the Agreement and Statements of Work but are silent on revoking this licence, and § 4(d) and § 7(c) confirm our continuing right to modify the delivered software after termination or final payment. The walk-away scenario (licence revocable at Vendor's discretion) is absent. Material term 2 - affiliates and contractors: the word "Affiliates" does not appear, but the express "right to grant a sublicense", read with the broad permitted purpose "in connection with Company's business operations", is a workable path to extend the licence to our affiliates and to contractors acting on our behalf. That defeats the walk-away test ("affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them") and reaches the fallback ("affiliates covered on written notice") in substance; the absent keyword is a phrasing variant, not a coverage gap. Material term 3 - successor transfer: the general non-assignment clause (p0042) requires the other party's consent but provides it "will not be unreasonably withheld", a practical route to a successor in an M&A transaction - again at the fallback rather than the preferred position. Shortfalls against the preferred wording are minor sub-elements noted here rather than flagged: no express "irrevocable", affiliates and contractors not named in the grant, and no explicit M&A carve-out from the assignment consent. Under the playbook's classification semantics a clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined, so flagging would be over-flagging. If § 4 or § 10 is reopened for other reasons, the low-cost asks are adding "irrevocable", inserting "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf", and carving M&A successors out of the p0042 consent requirement.
